claims.text: Filter by % Adj.
claims.note: The filter is set from the "% ADJ." link and tests each station's suggested percent adjust (sa-dashboard.component.ts:791). The dialog's own instruction reads "Filter % Adj. by setting an Over and/or Under threshold." (SPATIAL_ADJUST.FILTER_CFG_INSTRUCTIONS).

claims.text: Find the outliers at both ends before you push.
claims.note: One filter tests both ends at once.

claims.text: The Over/Under filter finds the extremes at both ends at once.
claims.note: With both ends enabled, a station is caught if its suggestion is above Over or below Under. When one end is disabled, that side falls back to a value no suggestion reaches (9999 for Over, 0 for Under), and the filter catches the other end only.

claims.text: It is not a range, and reading it as one will mislead you.
claims.note: The test is an OR of two strict comparisons, so the stations it shows lie outside the band, not inside it.

claims.text: Table toolbar
claims.note: The tabs and the filter link are the first item in the table toolbar (#sa-dit-toolbar) above the station table. The rest of that toolbar holds the applied target profile name and the Calculation ET readout (sa-dashboard.component.html:30-33).

claims.text: The filter reads the suggested percentage, and only for stations that are enabled.
claims.note: Retyped from prerequisite to behaviour. The test reads suggestedAdjAmtPercent, the calculated suggestion (sa-dashboard.component.ts:597), not the value typed into % Adj., so editing a station does not move it into or out of the filter. Disabled areas and holes are skipped as well as disabled stations (:771, :774, :790). On production saShowCurrentOnly is true (environment.toro-prod.ts:87), so a station is tested only when its scan is from today or its value is estimated (sa-dashboard.component.ts:789). A stale station under Option 1, which shows a dash in % Adj. (sa-table-card.component.html:51-62), is never caught.

claims.text: A disabled station never appears in it however extreme its number.
claims.note: A disabled station is never caught by its own number (sa-dashboard.component.ts:790), but it can still appear. The filter groups a hole's stations by name, and when any enabled member of a group is caught, the whole group goes into the filtered list, including a disabled partner (:785-795). The table shows a same-name group as one paired row with its stations beneath it (sa-dash-table.component.ts:186-253). Disabled areas and holes never appear (sa-dashboard.component.ts:771, :774).
claims.correction: A disabled station is never caught by its own number, however extreme. It appears only as part of a paired row whose enabled partner is caught. Why: the filter keeps a whole same-name group when any enabled member matches (sa-dashboard.component.ts:785-795).

claims.text: Read the two tabs
claims.note: Two tabs: All Stations and Over/Under.

claims.text: All Stations carries the full count.
claims.note: The count is the number of unique station names on the course. A paired station counts once, and disabled stations, holes and areas are included. It shows a dash only when the course has no stations.

claims.text: Beside it, the Over/Under tab carries the count of stations the filter currently catches.
claims.note: Counted by unique station name, like All Stations, so a caught paired row counts once.

claims.text: Until you set a filter that count is a dash and the tab does nothing — it is not broken, there is simply nothing to show yet.
claims.note: With neither end enabled the count is null. The tab shows "--", is styled disabled, and ignores clicks (sa-table-threshold-filter.component.ts:89). Saving with both ends unchecked also switches the table back to All Stations (:111-113). A filter that is set but catches nothing shows "--" as well, because the template prints the count or a dash (sa-table-threshold-filter.component.html:15), though that tab can then be selected.

claims.text: Two tabs: All Stations, and the Over/Under count.
claims.note: Figure caption. The labels are CASE_SENSITIVE.ALL_STATIONS "All Stations" and SPATIAL_ADJUST.FILTER_OVER_UNDER "Over/Under", each with its count. The Over/Under tab also carries an over/under icon.

claims.text: Open the options
claims.note: The filter link toggles the Over/Under Options dialog.

claims.text: The link to the right of the table toolbar states the thresholds currently in force — % ADJ.
claims.note: The readout is right but the location is not. The filter component stacks its contents in a column (sa-table-threshold-filter.component.less:8-11): the two tabs on top, and below them a row of two links, BULK ADJUST first and the filter link second (sa-table-threshold-filter.component.html:18-37). Nothing of the filter sits to the right of the table toolbar. The right of that toolbar holds the applied target profile name and the Calculation ET readout (sa-dashboard.component.html:30-33). The link text is upper-cased and starts "% ADJ." whenever either end is enabled (SPATIAL_ADJUST.PERCENT_ADJUST_OVER_UNDER, _OVER, _UNDER).
claims.correction: The link below the two tabs, beside Bulk Adjust, states the thresholds currently in force — % ADJ. Why: the tabs and the two links are stacked in a column, with BULK ADJUST first and the filter link second (sa-table-threshold-filter.component.html:18-37, sa-table-threshold-filter.component.less:8-11).

claims.text: OVER 200%, UNDER 10% — so you can read the filter without opening it.
claims.note: Retyped from navigation to label. With both ends enabled at the defaults, the link reads "% ADJ. OVER 200%, UNDER 10%" (SPATIAL_ADJUST.PERCENT_ADJUST_OVER_UNDER, upper-cased). With one end enabled it shows only that end ("% ADJ. OVER {{over}}%" or "% ADJ. UNDER {{under}}%"). With neither enabled it reads "APPLY A FILTER TO SEE RESULTS" (SPATIAL_ADJUST.FILTER_APPLY_FOR_RESULTS). A new user sees that last text, because both ends start disabled (sa-adjust-threshold.model.ts:9-10).

claims.text: Clicking it opens Over/Under Options.
claims.note: The dialog header is SPATIAL_ADJUST.OVER_UNDER_OPTIONS "Over/Under Options".

claims.text: The link doubles as a readout of the current thresholds.
claims.note: The text is rebuilt from the saved thresholds and shows only the ends that are enabled.

claims.text: Set the two ends independently
claims.note: Over and Under each have a checkbox and a number input.

claims.text: Over accepts 0 to 300 and defaults to 200.
claims.note: The input is bounded 0 to 300 in steps of 1, with a " %" suffix (sa-cfg-threshold-dlg.component.html:31-34). 200 is the default value, but the Over checkbox itself starts unticked (sa-adjust-threshold.model.ts:9).

claims.text: Under accepts 0 to 100 and defaults to 10.
claims.note: The input is bounded 0 to 100. 10 is the default value, and the Under checkbox also starts unticked (sa-adjust-threshold.model.ts:10).

claims.text: Each has its own checkbox, so you can run one end without the other — Over alone to find the stations asking for far too much, Under alone to find the ones asking for almost nothing.
claims.note: Each input is disabled while its checkbox is clear. A disabled end falls back to a value no suggestion reaches, so the filter runs on the other end alone.

claims.text: Over/Under Options.
claims.note: Figure caption. Under the header the dialog reads "Filter % Adj. by setting an Over and/or Under threshold." It saves with "Save Changes" (SPATIAL_ADJUST.SAVE_CHANGES) and closes with Cancel.

claims.text: Each threshold has its own checkbox.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: It catches both extremes, not a band
claims.note: The comparison is an OR across the two ends.

claims.text: A station is caught if its suggestion is above the Over value OR below the Under value.
claims.note: Both comparisons are strict, so a suggestion exactly at the Over or Under value is not caught. The value tested is the suggestion, not an edited % Adj. (see filter-adjustments/before/1).

claims.text: With 200 and 10 set you get everything over 200 percent and everything under 10 percent — and nothing in between.
claims.note: Because the comparisons are strict, 200 and 10 themselves fall in the middle band and are not shown.

claims.text: It is an outlier finder.
claims.note: It lists the stations outside the band at either end.

claims.text: Reading it as “between 10 and 200” gives you exactly the stations it is not showing you.
claims.note: Read as a range, the filter would show exactly the stations it leaves out.

claims.text: The filtered tab: the extremes at both ends, not the middle.
claims.note: Figure caption. The Over/Under tab renders the filtered list as a flat table (showFlatFilteredList).

claims.text: Why it matters. These are the two lists worth a second look before a push: the ones about to get a great deal of water, and the ones about to get almost none.
claims.note: Holds for the suggestions. The filter reads the calculated suggestion, so a station whose % Adj. has been edited is listed on its suggestion, not on the value that would be pushed (sa-dashboard.component.ts:597-598, sa-confirm-push-dlg.component.ts:74-79).

claims.text: Exclude Zeros belongs to Under
claims.note: The checkbox sits in the Under block of the dialog.

claims.text: Exclude Zeros is greyed out until Under is enabled, because a zero is below any under-threshold and the option means nothing without one.
claims.note: Disabled while Under is unchecked (sa-cfg-threshold-dlg.component.html:67). The reason given holds for any Under value above 0. At 0 the strict comparison catches nothing, zeros included.

claims.text: Tick it and genuine zeros drop out of the filter, leaving the stations that asked for a little rather than the ones that asked for nothing.
claims.note: With Exclude Zeros on, a station whose suggestion is exactly 0 is not caught. The saved setting is applied whether or not Under is enabled (sa-dashboard.component.ts:758, :792), but with Over alone it changes nothing, because 0 is never above the Over value.

claims.text: Your thresholds are saved to your own user preferences, not to the site.
claims.note: Saving writes the thresholds into the signed-in user's dashboard preferences (dashUserManager.updateDashUserPreferences) and shows "Threshold settings have been saved." Another user on the same site keeps their own thresholds.

claims.text: Exclude Zeros is disabled until Under is on.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: Not the same setting. Settings › Minimum Threshold has its own Exclude Zeros.
claims.note: Settings has a Minimum Threshold tab (sa-settings-dlg.component.ts:54). Its Exclude Zeros checkbox sits under the option "Set to the minimum threshold value when pushed to Lynx", and is enabled only with that option and a non-zero threshold (sa-settings-dlg.component.html:156-170).

claims.text: That one changes what gets written to Lynx at push time.
claims.note: With "Set to the minimum threshold value when pushed to Lynx" chosen, a pending station whose % Adj. is below the threshold is raised to it at push time. Exclude Zeros leaves stations at 0 alone (sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:448-452). The substitution is made on the push dialog's copy when the push is sent (sa-confirm-push-dlg.component.ts:74-79).

claims.text: This one only changes which rows you are looking at.
claims.note: The Over/Under Exclude Zeros is read only by the filter (sa-dashboard.component.ts:792). It is not part of what is pushed.

claims.text: You can state that the filter is an OR across both ends, not a range.
claims.note: Achievable from the guide.

claims.text: You know the Over/Under count reads as a dash until a filter is set.
claims.note: True until a filter is set. A set filter that catches nothing also shows a dash (see filter-adjustments/1/4).

claims.text: You know which Exclude Zeros changes the push and which only changes the view.
claims.note: Achievable from the guide.
